about.metaDescription: KanbanCord is a kanban board that lives in your Discord server: run it entirely with the bot, and use the website for the big picture and fine-tuning.
about.title: About {name}
about.p1: {name} is a kanban board that lives in your Discord server. The idea is simple: your community already talks in Discord, so planning should happen there too. Create boards and columns, add tasks, move them along, assign people, set labels, priorities and due dates, and discuss them in comments, all with the bot's slash commands, without leaving the chat. Updates arrive in the channels you choose and, for your own tasks, by direct message.
about.p2: Most people never need anything else. The website is there when you want the whole board at a glance, or to fine-tune things: detailed permissions per board and per person, the labels and priority levels a board offers, which features a server uses, exactly which updates you are told about, and the audit log of every change.
about.p3: It follows your server's Discord roles and permissions from the start, so the right people see and change the right boards without setting anything up twice.
about.madeBy: {name} is built and run by {operator}. It is free, has no ads, and does not sell or track your data (see the Privacy Policy). Found a problem or have an idea? Use /report in Discord. Questions, or want to hear about new features? Join the support server. If you would like to help with its costs, see Support.
about.find: {name} has its own page in <directory>Discord's App Directory</directory>, where you can add it to a server straight from Discord. Whether the website, the bot and everything behind them are running, and any planned maintenance, is on the <status>status page</status>.
about.start1: Add the bot to your server.
about.start2: Create a board with /board create, then add tasks with /task create.
about.start3: Run /help to see everything the bot can do.

support.metaDescription: KanbanCord is free for everyone. If you would like to help with its costs, you can leave a voluntary donation on Ko-fi.
support.title: Support {name}
support.p1: {name} is free, has no ads and no paid plans, and it will stay that way. It is a personal project, built and run by {operator}.
support.p2: If it is useful to your server and you would like to help with its costs, such as the domain, and the servers it will need if it grows, you can leave a donation on Ko-fi.
support.voluntary: Donations are entirely voluntary. Everyone gets the same {name}, whether they donate or not.
support.buysNothing: A donation does not buy features, limits, roles, priority support or anything else.
support.payments: Payments are handled by Ko-fi and PayPal, never by {name}. We do not link donations to your Discord account.
support.refunds: Donations are not refundable as a rule. If you donated by mistake, email <email>{email}</email> and we will do what we can.
support.notDonating: Not donating is completely fine. Telling others about {name}, or reporting a bug with /report, helps too.

faq.metaDescription: Answers about KanbanCord: pricing, adding the bot, permissions, Discord commands, notifications, uploads and your data.
faq.title: Frequently asked questions

free.a: Yes. There are no paid plans, no ads, and your data is not sold.

start.a: Add the bot, then run /guide in Discord for a step-by-step walkthrough. The guides cover everything from a shared to-do list to reminders and permissions.

website.a: No. {name} is built to be used entirely from Discord: create boards, columns and tasks, move and assign them, set labels, priorities and due dates, comment, and choose your notifications, all with slash commands. The website is for when you want the whole board at a glance, or to fine-tune settings.

add.q: How do I add it to my server?
add.a: Use "Add to Discord" at the bottom of any page, and pick the server. You need the Manage Server permission there. Then create a first board with /board create and add tasks with /task create.

access.q: Who can see and change my boards?
access.a: It follows your server's Discord roles and permissions by default: administrators and moderators can manage boards, members can work with tasks. Server administrators can change this for the whole server or per board, in the server and board settings.

servers.q: Why does signing in ask for my list of servers?
servers.a: So {name} can show which of your servers you can manage and add the bot to. It does not read your messages.

discord.q: What can I do from Discord?
discord.a: Everything you need day to day: create, view, rename and archive boards; add, rename, reorder and delete columns; create, edit, move and delete tasks; assign people and roles; set labels, priorities and due dates; read and write comments; choose your own notifications with /notifications; and, for server managers, set up update channels with /kanbancord. Run /help in Discord for every command.

websiteOnly.a: Fine-tuning and the big picture: seeing a whole board at once, permission rules per board and per person, the labels and priority levels a board offers, which features a server uses, exactly which updates you are told about, themes and accessibility options, uploading images and videos, and browsing the audit log.

notifications.a: A server can have the bot post updates in chosen channels, and mirror its audit log in one; update posts can show the whole task with buttons to move it, assign people or edit it right there. You can also get direct messages about tasks you are assigned to, created or follow, including reminders when they are due. If a channel already mentioned you about something, you do not get a direct message about it too. Choose what you get with /notifications, or in more detail under Settings → Notifications on the website. Server managers set up channels with /kanbancord.

uploads.q: Where are uploaded images and videos stored?
uploads.a: On Imgur. Anyone with the link can see them, so do not upload anything private.

data.q: How do I remove my data?
data.a: Sign out everywhere under Settings → Sessions, and ask us to delete the rest at <email>{email}</email>. Server administrators can delete boards, and removing the bot from a server stops it syncing that server. Details are in the <privacy>Privacy Policy</privacy>.

help.q: I found a bug, have an idea, or need help.
help.a: Join the {name} support server to ask questions and hear about new features, or use /report in Discord to send a report straight to the developer.
